seo.description: Learn how the Route du Rhum protects natural areas from Pointe du Grouin to Cap Fréhel as part of its CSR strategy.

sections.titre: From Pointe du Grouin to Cap Fréhel
A Protected Coastline, a Responsible Race

haut.chapo: From Pointe du Grouin to Cap Fréhel, the Route du Rhum passes along one of the most sensitive coastlines in Saint-Malo Bay. Protecting these areas is not an option: it is an obligation, and a conviction.

photo.alt: A rocky island covered in heathland in the middle of the bay, seen from the air, with sailboats offshore

options.texte: The best way to experience the thrill of the start is to be at the Race Village in Saint-Malo, among the fans, in front of the giant screens!
The second option is to watch the start on television from home, thanks to our partner France TV, which broadcasts the start live. It is the best way to watch the boats set off!

If you really want to watch the start from the coast, please note that Pointe du Meinga is closed to the public and that all sites from Pointe du Grouin to Cap Fréhel have restricted access; details are available further down this page.

texte: The Natura 2000 network aims to ensure the long-term survival of particularly vulnerable species and habitats. This European initiative, implemented in France, focuses on promoting the natural heritage of the regions.

Natura 2000 establishes measures for the protection of natural habitats and the management and regulation of bird species that naturally occur in the wild within the European territory of member states: these measures include prohibitions on their trade, collection, capture, and the degradation of their environment. Through Natura 2000, the European Union protects nearly 1,600 species of wild animals and plants, and more than 600 species of birds.

photo.alt: A cliff and its lighthouse above the sea, seen from the air

pourquoi.titre: A Protected Coastline, a Responsible Race
pourquoi.texte: As organizers, we must take all necessary measures to prevent damage to the natural areas through which the event passes. A consultation process is under way with local authorities and the managers of the areas concerned, including the Conservatoire du Littoral, the departmental authorities, the DDTM, site managers, the Grand Site de France Cap d’Erquy-Cap Fréhel and the Rance-Émeraude Regional Nature Park. In parallel, a Natura 2000 Impact Assessment (EIN) has been carried out with the Biotope agency.

carte.texte: The natural areas of Saint-Malo Bay are home to remarkable coastal biodiversity. Hosting a major sailing event must be done in a way that respects this ecological balance, year after year.
carte.chute: “This is also what links the Sustainability Pact to the rest of our CSR strategy: protecting the journey means protecting the destination.”

mesures.intro: This is a collaborative effort: it brings together government agencies (DDTM, Prefectures), the Conservatoire du Littoral, the departments of Ille-et-Vilaine and Côtes-d’Armor, the Brittany Region, and the Rance Émeraude Regional Nature Park, alongside our teams and a firm specializing in environmental issues. Our action plan is organized around four categories of measures.

liste.chapo: Protect the most sensitive areas and times.
liste.texte: Dedicated working groups at each sensitive site (Pointe du Grouin, Saint-Cast, Cap Fréhel) help anticipate and limit the event’s impact on natural environments.

photo.alt: The race boats lined up in the harbour basin at sunset

liste.chapo: Limit the event’s impact on natural environments.
liste.texte: The Hazard Reporting System and cetacean protection zones reduce the risk of collisions with marine wildlife offshore.

photo.alt: The walled city of Saint-Malo seen from the air, between the sea and the harbour basins

liste.chapo: Monitor and measure the race’s impact on biodiversity.
liste.texte: The action plan is being developed in collaboration with a firm specializing in environmental issues and in coordination with government agencies responsible for ensuring compliance with Natura 2000 regulations.

photo.alt: A work room, people wearing headphones in front of their computers

liste.chapo: Raise public awareness and promote best practices.
liste.texte: Volunteers are stationed in the busiest areas to raise public awareness and ensure that natural spaces are respected throughout the event.

photo.alt: A trimaran in the colours of Edmond de Rothschild, on the water

benevolat.texte: Public outreach, field monitoring: every volunteer contributes directly to coastal protection during the 13 days of the village. Find details on the two available volunteer opportunities in our dedicated fact sheets.
